youtube.title: What Is Actually Inside a Pore? | Skin Sense No. 015
youtube.caption:
Look closely at your skin. Those tiny dots... are pores.

Partway down sits a small oil gland. Its cells do something strange. vo: Each one slowly fills with oil... until the whole cell breaks down and becomes oil. That's a pore. A doorway. A hair. A gland. And its tiny residents. vo: Until... the doorway gets blocked.

Series: Season 1: The organ you live inside, part 15 of 6.

Sources
1. Visible skin pores are the openings of hair follicles (the pilosebaceous unit). — NCBI (NIH): https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK470321/
2. Sebaceous glands are attached to hair follicles and empty into the upper follicle. — NCBI (NIH): https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK499819
3. Cutibacterium acnes and other microbes live in the follicle and use sebum lipids (via lipases) as a food source. — f1000research.com: https://f1000research.com/articles/7-1953

Illustrations: AI-generated and 3-D animation made in code, no stock footage. Narration: a real person's voice (recorded, not AI). Every number is checked against the sources.
